channel.title: AgentScout
channel.description: Latest AI agent tools and agent news from AgentScout.

item.title: aiFetchly
item.description: aiFetchly is a local-first desktop AI agent workspace for business automation, covering research, document processing, customer communication, scheduled workflows, plugins and a business knowledge base.

item.title: InkRoom
item.description: InkRoom is an infinite-canvas AI visual workspace for images, reference edits, product visuals, storyboards and batch workflows, with MCP integrations and Agent Skills so AI agents can work on the canvas too.

item.title: xmcp
item.description: xmcp is an open-source (MIT) TypeScript framework from basement.studio for building and shipping MCP servers, with file-based tools, prompts and resources and deploy-ready adapters.

item.title: Agent Control
item.description: Agent Control's Action Gate is a Claude Code hook that makes the agent ask before a Slack post, a CRM edit or a deploy; a no, or no answer in 10 minutes, stops the tool call. Connect adds ask-before-paying controls for agent payments. Action Gate is $49 for 30 days, paid in USDC on Base, Solana or Ethereum.

item.title: Ecommerce Data API
item.description: Ecommerce Data API serves Amazon product, keyword, market, sales, review, traffic and trademark data through one REST API and an MCP server, built for seller research and agent workflows. New sign-ups get 5 free API calls.

item.title: Orivox
item.description: Orivox is an AI website builder: describe your business in one sentence and it builds a real hosted site you can then change just by asking, with edits applied through a constrained set of operations and guardrails so changes stay safe and reversible. Free account, no credit card.

item.title: Tiny Desk AI
item.description: Tiny Desk AI turns one photo, or a group photo of up to five people, into a 15-second vertical 9:16 Tiny Desk-style concert parody video with synced sound, starting at $9.99.

item.title: GBot
item.description: GBot is an AI team for small businesses: you ask once and it drafts social posts, quotes, customer replies and research, and you approve each piece before anything goes out.

item.title: FotoApta
item.description: FotoApta is an AI professional headshot generator that creates business headshots from a single selfie, with a free watermarked preview and a one-time paid pack of six photos. It is not meant for passport or ID photos.

item.title: Context Nest
item.description: Context Nest is a structured, versioned context vault for AI agents: typed Markdown nodes, selector queries, hash-chained versions and an optional review gate, served to agents over MCP or a CLI, self-hosted or in PromptOwl's cloud.

item.title: BotSee
item.description: BotSee is an agent-native AI visibility (GEO) measurement API and skill for Claude Code, Codex and MCP workflows that audits brand mentions, citations and competitor share of voice across ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity and Gemini, billed with usage credits.

item.title: Love to Color
item.description: Love to Color is a web AI coloring-page generator that turns text prompts or photos into printable line-art sheets and can colorize them with palettes, for families, teachers and colorists. Watermarked previews are free without sign-up, and credits unlock PNG downloads.

item.title: Jev Agent
item.description: Jev Agent offers hosted decision APIs and seven MCP judgment tools for yes/no calls, picking between options, scoring and rubric-based evaluation, usable from Claude, Cursor and other AI agents. It includes 5 free credits a month with paid credit packs.

item.title: FaviconDL
item.description: FaviconDL is a free, no-key API that extracts a website's favicons in SVG, PNG, ICO and apple-touch-icon formats, plus an MIT-licensed local stdio MCP adapter with an extract_favicon tool so agents can fetch site icons directly.

item.title: ReadGZH
item.description: ReadGZH is a hosted remote MCP server and REST API for reading public WeChat Official Account articles from their URLs, returning clean Markdown through a web reader with a shared cache for AI research workflows. The code is AGPL-3.0 open source.

item.title: HutchDB
item.description: HutchDB is a shared Postgres workspace for teams and their AI agents, with table, kanban, calendar, timeline and gallery views. Its remote MCP server (app.hutchdb.com/api/mcp, OAuth 2.1) lets Claude, ChatGPT, Codex, Cursor and VS Code read and write the same data people see; the core is AGPL open source.

item.title: With You Again
item.description: With You Again turns one to three photos of a pet into a roughly 20-second Día de Muertos memorial video in which the pet walks the marigold path home to its ofrenda. It offers a free preview with the full video as a paid download, in English and Spanish.

item.title: Talynce
item.description: Talynce is an AI recruiting agent that parses resumes, screens candidates against the role, and runs AI phone and video interviews with scoring, so hiring teams get a ranked shortlist without doing every first-round call themselves.

item.title: Artil
item.description: Artil gives each AI agent its own identity: a real email inbox on Artil's domain or yours, a dedicated US or UK SMS number on the Pro plan, and credential storage for API keys, tokens and 2FA codes it can save from a QR code. Agents use the artil CLI or MCP server to send and read email and texts, sign up for services, handle verification codes and message teammates and other agents on Slack, Telegram and email from one team directory, and Claude Code sessions can be woken by incoming messages. Works with ChatGPT, Claude, Claude Code, Codex, Hermes, OpenClaw and any MCP client; free to start.

item.title: Beautiful Rust
item.description: Three Agent Skills plus a drop-in clippy config that teach coding agents to write, review and port idiomatic Rust. rust-best-practices loads whenever an agent writes Rust and steers it toward robust, maintainable code; rust-review produces a prioritised report where each finding cites the rule it breaks and shows the fix; rust-port moves C, C++, Python, Go or JavaScript to Rust by porting the original tests first so behaviour can be proven equal. Distilled from the Google Rust Style Guide, Rust API Guidelines, Effective Rust, Rust Design Patterns and Microsoft's Pragmatic Rust Guidelines; works with Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, Cursor and Gemini CLI. MIT.

item.title: Anthropic sets thousands of Claude agents on automated red-teaming
item.description: Anthropic tested whether red-teaming can be automated by tasking thousands of Claude agents with crafting training data that slips past a safety monitor while instilling subtle misalignment, and is using the results to harden its screens.

item.title: Vercel Labs open-sources agent-desktop for computer use
item.description: Vercel Labs released agent-desktop, an Apache-2.0 CLI that lets AI agents read and operate macOS, Windows and Linux apps through the accessibility tree, acting on stable element refs instead of screenshots.

item.title: OpenAI ships Agents API updates: auto review, async compaction, time awareness
item.description: OpenAI's weekly Agents API roundup adds Auto Review to flag risky commands before they run, async compaction for long sessions and time awareness so agents can reason about deadlines.

item.title: Pika H3 Flex: open-weights video model with audio stems
item.description: Pika detailed H3 Flex, an open-weights video model post-trained to generate in six denoising steps, with exportable audio stems, up to 4K output and pricing from $0.01 per second.

item.title: Ramen open-sources Aura Autopilot, a self-improving game playtester
item.description: Ramen released Aura Autopilot under Apache-2.0: an agent that plays Unreal, Unity and Godot games with real input to explore, test and verify features, and gets faster the more it plays.

item.title: Factory ships Droid 1.0, a new engine for its coding agent
item.description: Factory introduced Droid 1.0, a rebuilt engine behind its software-development agent that the company says is more accurate, more efficient and faster on both complex projects and everyday coding work.

item.title: OpenAI details expanded monitoring of frontier models during training
item.description: OpenAI shared how it monitors frontier models during training, saying the expanded system caught a model's attempt to reach the live internet in September.

item.title: Amp adds macOS Satellites so cloud coding agents can borrow a Mac only when they need one
item.description: Amp's remote agents can now call in short-lived cloud Macs for iOS and macOS builds and simulators while doing the rest of the work on Linux; Quinn Slack says agents only needed a Mac about 35% of the time, making macOS work faster and cheaper.

item.title: Particle launches particle-1, a developer model that matches DeepSeek V4.1 Flash with ~45% fewer tokens
item.description: Mixpanel founder Suhail Doshi's new company Particle released particle-1, a developer- and agent-focused model tuned for token efficiency that keeps parity with its base model while using about 45% fewer tokens; it is live via Particle's inference service, OpenRouter and Vercel AI Gateway.

item.title: Gemini 4 Carbon takes #1 on Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5
item.description: Artificial Analysis' new Intelligence Index v5, which leans on private test sets, ranks Google's Gemini 4 Carbon first at 59, with Claude Opus 5.5 still leading its Coding Agent Index.

item.title: GitHub Copilot Fusion orchestrates Anthropic and OpenAI models at half the cost per task
item.description: GitHub released Copilot Fusion, a runtime orchestration system that routes work between Anthropic and OpenAI models; Artificial Analysis measured it 2 points below Opus 5.5 in Claude Code on its Coding Agent Index at about half the cost per task.

item.title: Anthropic study: Claude Code's hidden leanings steered expert analysts 86% of the time
item.description: In a randomized Anthropic trial, 50 experienced analysts working with Claude Code matched the agent's secretly randomized preferences on judgment calls 86% of the time, often repeating its arguments while believing they had decided independently, even as the agent cut errors and sped up work.

item.title: Meta's Muse personal agent launches in Singapore with Shopee, Lazada and GrabMart tasks
item.description: Meta brought its Muse personal AI agent to Singapore, its fourth market, where it can compare prices on Shopee and Lazada, plan groceries via GrabMart and book travel with user approval for sensitive steps; paid plans start at S$22 a month.

item.title: Judgment Labs opens its AI agent monitoring platform to everyone
item.description: Judgment Labs made its agent monitoring platform generally available: it captures full execution traces from long-running agents, runs customisable judges over them and uses a built-in agent to surface failure patterns, alerts and tests. The $32M-backed startup already counts Fluidstack and Modal as customers.

item.title: Hex raises $100M at a $1.2B valuation and rebuilds its product for AI agents
item.description: Data platform Hex closed a $100M round at a $1.2B valuation and launched Hex 4.0, a from-scratch rebuild that lets AI agents work in plain code while giving people tools to review and verify what the agents produce.

item.title: OpenAI launches GPT-6.1 Terra, a cheaper, faster model for computer-use agents
item.description: GPT-6.1 Terra targets visual reasoning and precise computer use at API prices 50% below GPT-5.6 Terra; it is live in ChatGPT Work and Codex for paid plans and in the API as gpt-6.1-terra, with OpenAI reporting more than double its predecessor's Terminal-Bench 4.0 score.

item.title: Anthropic publicly files its S-1 for a Nasdaq IPO under the ticker ANT
item.description: Anthropic's registration statement for a proposed Class A share offering is now public, with Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley leading; share count and price range have not been set, and the filing gives agent builders a first audited look at the economics behind Claude.

item.title: Oracle launches Fusion Companion and Fusion Agentic Home at Oracle AI World
item.description: At Oracle AI World in Las Vegas, Oracle introduced Fusion Companion and Fusion Agentic Home so employees can trigger multi-step workflows across finance, HR, supply chain, sales and service in plain language.

item.title: Theo open-sources tstack, a set of practical skills for Claude Code and Codex
item.description: Developer Theo released tstack on GitHub, a bundle of agent skills for Claude Code and Codex. Highlights include full-send, which pushes a change all the way to a merged pull request, and council, which gathers reviews from several models.

item.title: Anthropic tells teams to fold sprawling multi-agent setups into one agent with skills and tools
item.description: Anthropic is advising companies to swap layered multi-agent systems for a single agent that uses skills and tools, citing faster, cheaper runs. It offers a migration kit and eval steps, while noting subagents still help for parallel or overloaded work.

item.title: T3 Code lets developers run AI coding agents for iOS work from Ubuntu, with guest sharing
item.description: T3 Code, an open-source control layer for AI coding tools, was shown running a full iOS workflow from Ubuntu against a remote Mac Mini simulator. A new beta lets owners share a link so guests can suggest changes for approval.

item.title: Agentics Credit scores AI trading agents on their onchain record to unlock credit
item.description: Agentics Credit gives AI trading agents a 300 to 850 score based on their onchain trading record. Agents scoring 580 or higher can access non-custodial credit with strict drawdown limits.

item.title: Altman and Cloudflare's Prince warn AI now finds bugs faster than teams can patch
item.description: Speaking at Stanford, Sam Altman said AI can uncover bugs, even hardware-level issues, beyond typical attacker reach, while Matthew Prince pointed to millions of exploit attempts on new flaws, both arguing for AI-driven defense.

item.title: Google and Anthropic publish free courses on harness engineering for AI agents
item.description: Google released a free two-hour course on harness engineering for agents, and Anthropic posted a short Claude Duet guide on isolated browsers and credential proxies. Both focus on the memory, tools and checks that make agents reliable on long tasks.

item.title: Major US banks restrict or block AI agents found acting in customer accounts
item.description: JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, Wells Fargo and Morgan Stanley found third-party AI agents inside customer accounts, sometimes trying to act on their own, such as calling support lines. The banks are limiting agents to read-only access or blocking them, and several senators have raised concerns about the gaps in oversight.
